original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: In formal F2[S4] register circuits over three dirty scalar roles, determine the minimum paid-call count for diag([(13)(24)],[(13)(24)],[e]) using each of (12),(23),(34) at cost 1, all rank-one idempotents N over F2, and arbitrary free interleaved GL3(F2) scalar mixing; compare against direct cost 8.
scope_change_reason: The broader all-transposition permutation-rank formula duplicates the generic rank-one address argument already available for arbitrary affine registers, and the candidate D8 third-role extension has an exact UT3 follow-up in current Discussion records. Keep the accepted seed and nonabelian register question, but refine to a distinct rank-slack endpoint: two copies of the S4 double transposition have adjacent-transposition length 4 each but natural displacement rank 2 each. This makes a two-call sharing saving possible under the generous three-role alphabet, unlike the 4-cycle endpoint in PR #1720.
bottleneck_link: This tests whether nonabelian scalar-register mixing can exploit the gap between the Coxeter cost and natural displacement rank of a target. A saving would be a candidate bit mechanism requiring separate mapping into a supplier; the selected binding-only baseline currently reports the complex primitive as binding, so no selected kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Prove the even-call parity obstruction using the sign determinant over F2[C2], then enumerate the complete radius-three balls from identity and target over all 84 paid involutions. Stop after the exact meet result and direct word; do not widen the group, alphabet, or role count.
evidence: The direct formal endpoint costs 8 calls. The natural F2^4 permutation representation gives only a 4-call rank floor, while the sign determinant forces even length. Complete exact radius-three balls each contain 237474 formal 3x3 F2[S4] states with layers [1,84,4697,232692], hashes 050e8b23a52a22b845208eb0a241872e53511f7843dbf5c6e42b3eda4bc757ac and caf772096918c6a120a394f7f734667e9bf69d67a871f868d4063a848f87827a, and have empty intersection. Thus no word of length at most 6 exists and the exact minimum is 8 in this model. Eight call-omission controls, altered dirty-role control and all 84 factor involution checks pass. No supplier or kappa claim.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scoping, algebraic proof, exact search implementation, verification and writing. No subagents or independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can any supplier expose these adjacent transpositions as one uniformly paid operation while retaining the formal dirty-role endpoint?
